dedupe_keys.name: wildfire hazard potential whp map for the united states 2023 version

description: The Wildfire Hazard Potential map is a raster product of the USDA Forest Service that depicts the relative potential for high-intensity wildfire that may be difficult to manage, to inform wildfire hazard evaluation and fuels management priorities across very large landscapes. The 2023 version, released on 17 June 2024, builds on wildfire likelihood and intensity simulated with the Large Fire Simulator (FSim), fuels and vegetation data from LANDFIRE 2020 and point locations of past fires from about 1992 to 2020, and covers the United States at 270 metre resolution as continuous values and as five classes from very low to very high. It is produced by the Fire Modeling Institute at the Missoula Fire Sciences Laboratory. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY (Forest Service Research Data Archive datasets are released under CC BY). Access is free of charge. Caveats: WHP is not a forecast and does not show burn probability for a given year. It supports wildfire exposure screening of power lines, roads, water supply catchments and communities; a related record is the SILVIS wildland-urban interface change maps.
